text:
dave: Heads up — I ran a perf sweep on the nightly canary and found a regression when continuous batching is on + the architecture-aware kernel selector changes mid-request.

maria: can you paste the profile? which model and seqlen distribution?

dave: model=redwood-7B-v2-qat, workload=chat-like (median seq 80, p95 320). Here's the hot path excerpt from `perf-bot` pprof dump:
```
CPU: 98% 
Total samples 120s
  runtime.launch_kernel  28% 
  kernel_selector.choose   22% 
  batch_coordinator.wait  15% 
  kv_cache.populate        12% 
  compute_attention       10%
  other                   13%
```
Notably `launch_kernel` spikes when selector flips kernel types for mid-flight requests (small->large seq path).

alex: interesting. so continuous batching groups a mix of short+long and the selector then picks a heavier kernel for the long one, causing launch overhead for others?

dave: exactly. The selector currently picks per-request at dispatch time based on observed seqlen and device perf table. But we see churn: within a batch, requests start as appearing short but extend, so the kernel choice flips and causes re-launches and KV cache thrashing.

jen: any quick mitigations we can try on canary? e.g., lock kernel choice per-session, or add hysteresis in selector decisions?

maria: we pushed a small hysteresis earlier for quantized kernels but it was per model global. We could do per-request delay: if predicted tail growth > X, bias toward the lower-launch-overhead kernel.

dave: I rolled a debug patch that biases by predicted remaining tokens. Config snippet:
```json
{"continuous_batching": true,
 "selector_hysteresis_ms": 30,
 "seqlen_growth_threshold": 0.6,
 "prefer_low_launch_overhead": true}
```
Results: median latency +3ms, p95 down 14% and launch_kernel samples drop ~40%. But KV cache misses increased for long tails.

alex: can we pre-warm KV cache for requests predicted to grow? maybe speculative kv.populate for sessions above threshold. That way kernel keeps low-launch path and KV warmed for tails. Cost tradeoff though.

dave: tried speculative warmup in the local run: `kv_cache.populate(async=true, tokens=predicted_tail)` — p95 improved further but cost (tokens touched) up ~8%. Worth testing in staging.

perf-bot: Automated regression check: canary -> baseline diff: overall throughput -1.2%, median latency +2.1ms, p95 latency -12.4%, ops cost +0.9%.

maria: OK that matches manual runs. For long-term fix I propose: 1) selector hysteresis + per-session lock for accepted kernel for first N tokens, 2) speculative kv warmup when tail growth probability > 0.5, 3) introduce a lightweight micro-kernel option for short tails that has near-zero launch cost but slightly lower per-token efficiency.

alex: micro-kernel is neat but heavy lift. We should also improve telemetry: emit `selector_decision_reason` and `kernel_swap_count` per request to correlate.

jen: agree on telemetry. Also add a SLO alert that watches `kernel_swap_count > 0.1` (per 1k requests) because swapping is clearly correlated with latency spikes.

dave: I'll queue a three-pronged RFC: behavioral hysteresis + speculative kv warmup + telemetry. I'll add perf experiments to validate cost tradeoffs.

maria: small note — make sure the hysteresis respects dedicated GPU pools; their kernel launch cost is different so thresholds should be per-device-class.

dave: yep will parameterize by device class and topology.

alex: can we also add an experiment that forces continuous batching to only batch similar predicted-final-seqlen windows? Like a soft affinity hash on predicted final length. That reduces mixing.

dave: good call — will add affinity bucket experiment. That may reduce batching efficiency but could reduce kernel churn.

jen: thanks — please paste the RFC link here when ready. Also cc @ops for cost signoff if speculative warmup lands. :thumbsup:

dave: RFC draft here: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/1934516789-contbatch-kernel-autotune. Will tag ops + data.

alex: awesome. if you want I can help with the p95 test harness to simulate mixed tails at scale.

dave: that'd be great, thanks!

perf-bot: Note: rolling canary will run the affinity-bucket experiment at 10% traffic. Monitoring dashboards: /d/launch-kernel, /d/kv-cache-hits

maria: leaving action items: dave->RFC + staging runs, alex->harness, jen->alert thresholds, perf-bot->track experiment.

dave: sounds good. short follow-up: anyone see obvious pitfalls with per-session kernel locks? e.g., fairness or starvation?

alex: we might cause head-of-line blocking on devices with strict capacity if many sessions lock to expensive kernels. throttling needed.

maria: add admission control: allow locks only if queue depth < X or predicted cost budget available.

dave: noted. ok wrapping up — will ping when RFC is live. thanks all. :party:
